title: Train / flight seat booking (IRCTC, Cleartrip)
prompt: Search trains/flights by route+date, show seat availability, book and cancel seats. Train variant: a seat can be re-sold for a later segment (A->B then C->D). Flight variant: flights on sectors, several fare types, each with its own seat list, users pay from a fund balance.
followups: fair handling of concurrent bookings for the same seat (pessimistic vs optimistic locking)
segment-wise seat reuse on a train
DB schema for trains/routes/seats/bookings (+ payments table)
notes: Most-reported NEW problem. Zepto/InMobi/Walmart asked it as an LLD round (classes+schema+locking); Cleartrip as a 90-min runnable machine-coding problem (flight inventory); MMT and Navi in design rounds that went down to schema and booking algorithm.

title: Task / job scheduler (delayed, recurring, dependencies)
prompt: Accept jobs with a run time (epoch or cron-like), execute them when due; later parts add recurring schedules, priorities, dependencies and retries.
followups: priority ordering; retry up to N failures
cancel a task and its dependents
parallel execution with a worker pool
recurring intervals and 'run at time T' (Harness)
build it as a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor with a DelayQueue (Uber/GS)
place jobs on clusters that satisfy CPU/RAM needs (Arcesium)
notes: Swiggy Instamart phrased it as 'design your own cron: unix command + epoch time'. Uber and MPL mixed LLD with HLD in the same hour. Closest existing pages: mt-blocking-queue, mt-producer-consumer.

title: Inventory + order management (block, confirm, release stock)
prompt: addProduct / getStock / createOrder / confirmOrder: creating an order blocks stock, confirming deducts it, an unconfirmed block expires (e.g. after 5 minutes). Some versions split internal stock from external-seller stock reached via APIs.
followups: thread safety under many concurrent buyers (Meesho: 10M users, 5M products)
how the locking changes when the service is distributed (PhonePe review round)
notes: Meesho's signature machine-coding problem (3 reports, SDE-1 to SDE-3). PhonePe gave it with only 1 hour to code. Aggregator codezym also tags it for Flipkart, Intuit, TikTok, DE Shaw, Amazon (weak).

title: Shopping cart / marketplace checkout (with discounts)
prompt: Users browse products, add/remove items in a cart, see totals, check out into an order, see order history. Richer versions validate stock, apply discounts, take payment through a pluggable interface and send notifications.
followups: inventory validation and locking during checkout
notes: A stand-alone 'coupon / offers engine' was NOT found as its own first-hand question; discounts show up as one requirement inside cart, wallet (PhonePe offers) or billing problems. Codezym lists 'Billing and discounts system' for Flipkart/Cleartrip (aggregator only).

title: Library / book-lending system
prompt: Catalog books (several copies each), register members, borrow and return, limit books per member, list/filter books by author or availability. Flipkart's version adds a FIFO waitlist and late fines.
followups: FIFO waitlist: a returned copy is held for the first waiting member
generated IDs like ROW1234 (author prefix + number)
notes: Walmart asked it in the 'Java + LLD' round as design-only; Flipkart as a 90-minute runnable machine-coding drive.

title: Conference / meeting room booking
prompt: Rooms spread over buildings and floors; book a room for a time slot, list free rooms, cancel. Uber's short version: scheduleMeeting(start,end) returns a reservation id with a room, or an error.
followups: interval overlap check (sorted map per room)
max booking length (12h) and invalid-input errors
concurrent bookings of the same room
notes: Uber candidate was told it was 'a data-structure question' inside the LLD round and was rejected for over/under-structuring. Overlaps heavily with calendar (below).

title: Stock broker / trading app with portfolio (Zerodha, Groww)
prompt: Onboard users, list stocks, buy and sell, show each user's portfolio and transaction history. Flipkart's version adds market open/close and a limited 'time shift' that moves prices randomly.
followups: add stocks only while market is open
time-shift operation at most 10 times a day with bounded random price change
DB schema + APIs (Tekion, pen and paper)
notes: Different from the order-book slug: here there is no matching of buyers and sellers, the app trades against a price feed. Groww/Hotstar/Meesho asked the matching version (see order-book variants).

title: Social network / news feed (Twitter, Instagram) + comments
prompt: Users post, follow, reply, up/down-vote; show a personalised feed ranked by follow, score, replies and recency. Variants: hashtag follows (Gojek), comment threads with one reply level and annotations (Postman).
followups: feed ranking rules (followed users first, then score, replies, freshness)
influencer vs user roles, follow hashtags
Twitter LLD then HLD in the same round (PhonePe)
notes: Flipkart's hiring-drive version is a full 90-min runnable console app; Postman's comment system was coded in a Google Doc.

title: Task / issue tracker (Jira, Trello, sprint planner)
prompt: Create tasks/stories/bugs, assign to users, move through statuses, group into sprints; keep an activity log of every change.
followups: a user can hold at most 2 in-progress tickets even under concurrent edits (Meesho)
notes: Flipkart candidate was marked down for putting sprint and task logic in one class and for one enum per model.

title: URL shortener as LLD / machine coding
prompt: createURL(originalUrl, user, expiryDays) -> short code; resolve; expire. Postman asks for a small working API.
notes: Usually an HLD topic; these five reports treat it as class design + code.

title: Leaderboard service (games, contests, ratings)
prompt: Accept score submissions and return top-N / a user's rank. PhonePe: daily leaderboards for several games, campaign configuration, full and partial rank lists, result computation, concurrent submissions.
followups: top-N contestants and top-N departments (PhonePe hackathon variant)
average rating per user printed in descending order (Atlassian agent-rating variant)
notes: Mixed depth: PhonePe is a coded machine-coding problem; Groww/Gojek/Games24x7 were design discussions. Codezym also lists 'Leaderboard for fantasy teams' and 'Customer support agent rating leaderboard' (aggregator).

title: Calendar / meeting scheduler with recurring events (Google Calendar)
prompt: Create events with location/start/end, recurring events (daily/weekly), share with view/edit permission, find a common free time across people and rooms, propose changes, list conflicts.
followups: find free time using others' availability and room availability
store recurring rules vs expanded instances
judged on class + DB + API design (Zepto)
notes: Zepto SDE-3 favourite in 2024 (LLD rounds run by InterviewVector). Zepto calendar posts may include 2 posts by one candidate; counted as 4 conservatively for Zepto incl. the Nov-2024 meeting scheduler.

title: Vehicle / car / bike rental
prompt: Branches with vehicle types, book by hourly slot at a fixed price, default choice = lowest price, fall back to another branch when none is free, system view of booked and free vehicles.
followups: reservations + car inventory as two services (Uber)

title: Hotel booking
prompt: Search hotels, view available rooms, reserve, manage bookings.
followups: concurrent reservation of the last room; ACID / isolation levels (Cars24)
notes: Both were LLD rounds run by third-party interviewers (InterviewVector). Agoda asks Booking.com-style search/booking only as HLD.

title: Doctor appointment booking (Practo)
prompt: Doctors register with a speciality and open 30-minute slots (9am-9pm); patients search by speciality, book and cancel; a patient cannot hold two appointments in the same slot.
followups: ranked slot list with a pluggable ranking strategy (start time, doctor rating)
waitlist: first waiting patient gets a freed slot
concurrency when two patients book the same slot (Flipkart review round)
notes: Agoda asked 'doctor appointment booking app' only as an architecture/HLD prompt (2025).

title: Gym / fitness class slot booking
prompt: Admins create classes with capacity and time; members book, cancel, list bookings; no overbooking, no overlapping bookings for one member.
followups: cancel only up to 30 min before start
staged requirements: Stage 1 must be fully working before Stage 2 (Udaan)
notes: Codezym lists a Flipkart 'Gym fitness center / FlipFit' version (aggregator only).

title: Customer-support issue / ticket assignment
prompt: Tickets arrive with a category; agents have skills in several categories; assign each ticket to a free capable agent; track agent work history and each ticket's phase.
followups: queue when no agent is free, retry

title: Delivery partner assignment (quick commerce, P2P parcel)
prompt: Onboard customers and delivery partners; auto-assign each order to an available partner, queue orders when none is free; pick-up, deliver, cancel rules; show order and partner status.
followups: notify via a mocked email/SMS vendor (bonus)
route optimisation using third-party real-time data (Zepto)
notes: Flipkart SDE-3 (Peer-to-peer delivery like Dunzo) and 'Flipkart Minutes' 2026. Existing food-delivery page covers restaurant-side assignment but not a driver pool.

title: In-memory document search engine
prompt: Create datasets, insert/delete text documents, search by keywords/pattern, order results (document size, keyword frequency, recency).
followups: AI tools allowed; judged on AI usage too (Razorpay 2026)
notes: Razorpay's most repeated senior machine-coding problem 2024-2026.

title: Circuit breaker
prompt: Wrap calls to a remote service: CLOSED -> OPEN after N failures, HALF_OPEN after a timeout, close again on success.
followups: store/replay requests while the service is down (Blinkit)
notes: Wise's 60-minute HackerRank pair-programming problem (3 reports incl. Hyderabad 2026).

title: Rule / expression engine
prompt: Evaluate business rules against records: Rippling = list of expense rules (total cap, per-seller-type cap, banned expense types) -> flag violations; Groww = evaluate a boolean expression string over a map of values.
followups: add new rule types / operators without touching existing code

title: Feature flags / staged app-version rollout
prompt: Microsoft: design a feature flag system. PhonePe: app-version management — apps have versions with minimum OS, admins roll out install/update by strategy (beta devices, percentage), updates ship a diff.
notes: PhonePe's version was coded from scratch on CodeSignal (2 reports).

title: Document manager with versions / Google Docs with ACL
prompt: Create, update, view, delete text documents; keep every version and revert; only the owner edits; Razorpay/Microsoft asked Google Docs with access control.

title: Resource / cluster allocation for tasks
prompt: Track servers (CPU config, price) in data centres or clusters and place tasks on single or multiple instances that meet the requirement; Microsoft: keep several containers running.

title: Snake game (Nokia-style, not snake & ladder)
prompt: Grid, snake moves each tick, eats food and grows, dies on wall/self collision; print head and tail positions.
followups: O(1) move with a deque + set
unit tests and exception handling are scored (Atlassian no-hire without them)

title: Tagging / activity-tag system
prompt: PhonePe machine coding: add hierarchical tags to activities and count how often each tag is used across entities. Atlassian/Salesforce: tags across products (Jira, Confluence) with API + schema.
notes: Only PhonePe's is a coded LLD; Atlassian's is its standard HLD question that drifts into schema/API detail.

title: User journey / workflow state machine
prompt: PhonePe: journeys are DAGs of stages; users onboard once and move to the next stage when events match rules; journeys are time-bound or perpetual and must be activated. Salesforce: log state transitions of workflow steps.
followups: mark time-bound journeys inactive after validity

title: Load balancer (working service)
prompt: Razorpay: a REST app with config endpoints (add/remove backend, timeouts, health checks) that proxies all other routes to mocked backends using a pluggable algorithm. Media.net SRE: TCP key-value server, then add a proxy, then a load balancer.
notes: Media.net's was an SRE loop.

title: Ludo / board game
prompt: Model a multi-player board game (Ludo) with turns, dice and pieces.
followups: Scrabble asked first at Urban Company

title: Thread pool / scheduled executor from scratch
prompt: Implement a ThreadPoolExecutor: worker threads, a blocking task queue, core vs max pool size, keep-alive, rejection policies, graceful shutdown. Uber/GS/Rubrik version: ScheduledExecutorService on a DelayQueue.
notes: First-hand only at Walmart; the Uber/GS/Rubrik claim comes from a compiled solution post (secondhand).

title: Online auction (highest unique bid) / BidBlitz
prompt: Sellers create auctions with min/max bid limits and a participation cost; buyers bid, update or withdraw; on close the highest UNIQUE bid wins; seller profit = winning bid + 20% of participation fees - average of limits. 2023 variant: lowest bid with SuperCoins wins a daily item.
followups: preferred buyer (>2 past auctions) wins ties (bonus)
notes: Flipkart signature.

title: Buy Now Pay Later (Flipkart BNPL)
prompt: Seed and view inventory; users have a credit limit; buy now, clear dues within 30 days; view dues and history.
notes: Flipkart signature; still live in June and Sept 2026 drives.

title: Bug bounty program manager
prompt: Employees log bug reports received by email, assign them, move through statuses (Open ... BountyPaid, Closed), edit, comment; admins delete.
notes: Flipkart signature (codezym lists it too).

title: Hackathon platform
prompt: Contestants (with department) solve problems (tag, difficulty, score); filter and sort problems; per-problem solver counts and average time; pluggable scoring; leaderboards for top contestants and top departments.
followups: recommend top-5 related problems after a solve (extension)
notes: PhonePe signature; interviewer who explains is not the one who evaluates.

title: Microprocessor / register machine simulator
prompt: Registers A-D and commands like SET, ADD, INR, MOV, PRINT read as text; implement the machine so new commands plug in.
followups: pre-written unit tests and model classes on HackerRank (2024)
notes: CRED signature.

title: In-memory loan EMI calculator
prompt: Model loans and compute EMIs; completed with bonus requirements.
notes: PDE (product development engineer) track.

title: Git-like version control
prompt: Implement init, add <regex>, checkout -b, reset HEAD~n, commit -m/-am, status, log, diff, help with extensible code.
followups: AI code assistant allowed in the proctored assessment

title: Middleware router with wildcards
prompt: put(path, value) / get(path) where get supports '*' segments (e.g. /a/*/c).
followups: hash map vs trie vs regex
notes: Atlassian code-design signature.

title: Subscription cost calculator
prompt: Products priced per month (JIRA $10, CONFLUENCE $7.5, BITBUCKET $8); users subscribe to combinations; compute monthly billing for a year.
followups: extensibility scoring ('how many lines change for a new requirement')
notes: Subscription billing at Razorpay, PhonePe and Groww was asked only as HLD.

title: Employee / team directory
prompt: Add employee, assign manager, add to team, show the hierarchy under anyone, roll up employee and team CTC; 2026 version: get/changeManager/addEmployee with at least two O(1) operations.
notes: Uber signature.

title: Train-to-platform assignment
prompt: Assign trains to platforms by schedule; query which train is on a platform at time t and which platform a train is on.
followups: min-heap assignment strategy vs random strategy
notes: Uber signature.

title: Employee access / resource manager
prompt: grant, revoke, get access for employees to resources; add/remove resources.
notes: Rippling signature (SDE-1 LLD round).

title: Music player analytics
prompt: add_song, play_song(user, song), print songs ranked by unique listeners, recently played unique songs per user (last k).

title: Delivery cost tracker
prompt: add_driver, add_delivery(driver, start, end), total cost; then pay_up_to(time) and cost still unpaid; then max active drivers in the last 24h.
notes: Rippling signature.

title: Amazon locker system
prompt: Assign parcels to lockers by size, pickup codes, expiry.

title: Medical crowdfunding
prompt: Patients raise several campaigns, donors donate to many campaigns, track campaign status; coded in 90 minutes on-site.

title: Survey builder (SurveyMonkey)
prompt: Surveys, questions, responses with API design and schema.

title: Reviews and ratings (user-generated content)
prompt: Post reviews/ratings, censor bad content, compute average rating; classes + schema.
followups: where censoring sits in the flow

title: Package tracking
prompt: Track shipments through checkpoints.
followups: multithreading and locks questions in the same round

title: Generic connection / resource pool
prompt: Hand out connections from a bounded pool (thread pool, DB pool); callers wait when empty.
followups: interviewer wanted code in the IDE straight away

title: Tree of Space: lock / unlock / upgrade on an M-ary tree
prompt: Lock(X,uid) fails if any ancestor or descendant is locked; Unlock; Upgrade(X,uid) replaces descendant locks held by uid with a lock on X. Part B: make it thread-safe without locking the whole tree.
followups: per-node mutexes / atomics instead of one global lock
race when two descendants notify the same ancestor
notes: Juspay hackathon: Part A 2h, Part B 8h over Slack.

title: On-call roster (PagerDuty-like)
prompt: Employee roster / rotation management.
notes: Pen and paper, in person.

title: Air traffic control: runway assignment
prompt: Planes request land, takeoff, dock, undock; runways used by one plane at a time, first come first served; fast in-memory structures plus persistence.

title: ChatGPT-style chat with context management
prompt: Users keep many chats and resume old ones; the model keeps no memory, so the service must build the right context for each prompt; classes, APIs, DB.

title: Live log tail (tail -f) server
prompt: Server watches a multi-GB append-only log, pushes new lines to many web clients, shows last 10 lines without re-reading the file.
followups: read last 10 lines by seeking from the end

title: Goal-tracking library with gamification
prompt: Break long-term goals into tasks; points, streaks, badges, leaderboards.
notes: Microsoft hiring drive; same candidate also got Google Docs.

title: Autocomplete engine
prompt: Return top-k suggestions for a prefix, update frequencies.
notes: Weak: one secondhand, one data-structure screen.

title: Google Classroom
prompt: Teachers, students, subjects/classes.

title: Undo delete with TTL (Postman collections)
prompt: Deleted collections can be restored for a limited time.
notes: Same loop: read the pickleDB code, split the big class, add TTL.

title: Chat application (WhatsApp) as LLD
prompt: One-to-one/group messages, delivery state; plus a separate multithreading coding question.
notes: Elsewhere chat is asked as HLD (Uber staff, Agoda, Amazon), not LLD.

title: Fantasy team selection validator (Dream11)
prompt: User has credits; pick exactly X players; min/max per category (keeper, batter...); at most Y from one real team; validate each pick.
notes: Asked in a frontend (React Native) loop. Codezym's 'Leaderboard for fantasy teams' is aggregator-only.

title: Cricket scoring / match simulator (Cricbuzz)
prompt: Simulate or score a short match: overs, balls, runs, wickets, strike change, extras.
notes: Only one in-window report and it is a mobile role; the classic Swiggy 'design Cricbuzz' report is from 2022 (outside window).

title: Agoda platform round: review a given Java service
prompt: Given a supplier/vendor search or booking service in Java, review it like a PR, then design APIs, cache keys (productId, vendorId) and indexes; refactor vendor calls behind a Strategy interface.
notes: Agoda signature (Bangkok + Gurugram).

title: Stripe multi-part practical (payments / fraud validation)
prompt: Multi-part coding on realistic payment data: validate records, extract features, compute a match ratio, return specific error codes; onsite adds Integration (call a live API) and Bug Bash (fix a failing test in an unfamiliar repo).
followups: each part builds on the previous one
notes: Not LLD in the Indian sense; included because Stripe Singapore/Bangalore use this loop.

title: Rank teams by votes (code-design framing)
prompt: Rank candidates/teams from ballots by position counts with tie-breaks, then extend (e.g., distributed or multithreaded counting).
followups: small LLD for rank computation with threads
notes: Essentially LeetCode 1366 asked inside Atlassian's coding / code-design loop.

title: Splitwise (expense sharing)
prompt: Add expenses split among users; per-user balances; simplified who-owes-whom.
followups: equal only, but extensible to exact/percent (Razorpay)
sample test cases verified by interviewer (Swiggy, ~3h incl. explanation)
notes: Still the single most repeated machine-coding problem in India.

title: Parking lot
prompt: Multi-level lot, slots by vehicle type, park/unpark, tickets, payment.
followups: slots reservable by several companies over time intervals (Swiggy 2026)
payment + switch to a subscription model (Flipkart)
different parking strategies and pricing models (Amazon)
extend a given parking-lot codebase with missing commands + tests (Gojek)

title: Rate limiter
prompt: Allow/deny requests per client using a pluggable algorithm.
followups: sliding window and leaky bucket both coded (Swiggy bar raiser)

title: Movie ticket booking (BookMyShow)
prompt: Theatres, shows, seats, booking.
followups: LLD then HLD in one round: actors, models, APIs, schema (Flipkart design round)

title: Notification system
prompt: Send notifications over channels based on events and preferences.
followups: stakeholder-specific rules: customer gets every status, seller only 'placed', logistics only 'shipped' (Cleartrip)
HLD + LLD skeleton code + schema in 90 min (Ola)
UML on draw.io, trade-offs over code (Blinkit)
notes: Cleartrip panel rejected a Kafka-style design: they wanted a demoable solution, not a scalable one.

title: Stock exchange order matching
prompt: Buy/sell orders matched by price-time priority.
followups: store matched orders in a table
notes: No first-hand Binance/OKX/Crypto.com report was found.

title: Pub-sub / Kafka-like queue
prompt: Topics, publishers, subscribers.
followups: per-consumer offset and in-order guaranteed delivery
what to do when a consumer is down; spill to disk and restore (plus points)

title: Ride sharing / cab booking
prompt: Riders, drivers, matching, trips.
followups: offer a ride vs take a ride, select by preference (Swiggy/MMT car-pool version)
nearest five drivers, first come first served, route history (Nykaa)
calculateETA by vehicle type via strategy (Paytm)

title: Food ordering (restaurants with capacity)
prompt: Restaurants with menus and capacity; orders auto-assigned by a strategy.
followups: selection strategy chosen by customer (lowest cost / best rating)
process commands sorted by timestamp even if given out of order (FoodKart)
notes: Flipkart evaluator 'cared more about features working than patterns' (2025).

title: In-memory DB / key-value store (transactions, TTL)
prompt: Tables or KV pairs with CRUD, then transactions or TTL.
followups: typed columns with constraints (string <= 20 chars, int >= 1024) and filters (Razorpay)
CodeSignal levels: CRUD -> prefix search -> TTL at a timestamp -> ... (Coinbase)
read pickleDB, split the god-class, add TTL (Postman)

title: LRU / LFU / in-memory cache
prompt: Bounded cache with eviction.
followups: evict by a rank from a mocked API, LRU as tie-break (LinkedIn)
two-level cache: per-user L1 (5) + global L2 (20) (Cleartrip ZipReel)

title: Expiring counter / TTL structures
prompt: Counts or values that expire after t seconds.
followups: event store with 1-minute timeout using a heap (Coinbase)

title: Snake and ladder
prompt: Board game with snakes, ladders, dice, players.
followups: config file: N players, board size, S snakes, L ladders, D dice
landing on an occupied cell sends that player back to 1
extra rules added live in the evaluation round

title: In-memory file system
prompt: mkdir, cd, ls, pwd, touch.
followups: cd with '*' matching '.', '..' or any child (Uber)

title: Q&A platform (Stack Overflow / Flipkart Overflow)
prompt: Topics, questions, answers, votes, feed.
followups: subscribe to topics; feed filtered by topic / answered / unanswered

title: Elevator
prompt: Lifts, requests, scheduling.

title: Vending machine
prompt: States, coins, inventory.

title: Logger
prompt: Levels, sinks, formatting.

title: Tic-tac-toe
prompt: Board, players, win check.

title: Payment gateway
prompt: Clients, pay modes, bank routing.
followups: router with distribution percentages across banks
switch traffic dynamically by bank success rate (extension)
notes: PhonePe signature.

title: Digital wallet
prompt: Top-up, P2P transfer, balance, history.
followups: sort and filter transaction history (extensible sorters/filters)
notes: No CRED wallet/cashback LLD was found; CRED asks the microprocessor problem.

title: Text editor with undo/redo
prompt: append, backspace, undo, redo.
followups: redo only valid right after undo/redo

title: Spreadsheet
prompt: Cells, formulas.

title: Banking system (OOP coding)
prompt: Accounts, deposits, withdrawals, transfers.
followups: asked inside the DSA round as OOP code in Java

title: Small concurrency asks (thread-safe builder, multi-threaded fetch)
prompt: Thread-safe builder; multi-threaded page download + count.
followups: builder made thread-safe with atomics, not synchronized (MMT)
several threads fetch HTML and count a word, with communication between them (MMT)
notes: Maps loosely to the mt-* pages; no first-hand report of print-series, H2O or dining philosophers was found in this window.
